verses.note: God creates by speaking. The first thing Scripture shows about God's word is that it is effective: it does what it says. That conviction stands behind the prophets' "Thus says the LORD" and John's description of Christ as the Word.

The scene turns on the exact wording of God's word. Once the command is shrunk in generosity, sharpened in strictness, and softened in consequence, it is easier to set aside. Interpreters differ on whether ‘or touch it’ is a distortion or a well-meant fence around the command, but either way the conversation is now about a reshaped word.

God reveals his purpose to Noah before he acts. Amos 3:7 states the principle that the Lord does nothing without revealing his plan to his servants the prophets, and Peter calls Noah a preacher of righteousness (2 Peter 2:5).

The first time Scripture says the word of the LORD ‘came’ to someone, it comes to Abram in a vision. The prophetic word begins with the promise to Abraham, which is why later prophets keep returning to it.

God chooses to disclose his intentions to Abraham before acting. Amos 3:7 states the principle, and Jesus calls his disciples friends because he has made known to them what he heard from the Father (John 15:15). Abraham is called God's friend (2 Chronicles 20:7, Isaiah 41:8, James 2:23).
God speaks directly to a king outside the covenant family. Revelation in Genesis is not confined to the chosen line, even though its purpose here is to protect that line.

God speaks first and names himself before he asks anything. Jacob has done nothing to seek him, and the God who speaks identifies himself by his history with Jacob's family, so revelation comes as the continuation of promises already made.
